title: I Forwarded the Family Venmo Note After They Called It a Loan

parts.text: I opened Venmo at 2:14 p.m. and cousin Amber's $400 from March still said rent help, thanks, pay when you can. Now she was telling the family chat I owed interest because it was a loan. I was twenty-nine, graphic designer, holding a screenshot of her own note. Pay when you can is not APR. I forwarded the Venmo to the chat with no caption. Aunt Linda typed we do not screenshot money. The note was a screenshot of her daughter's words. At 2:19 Amber changed the Venmo privacy to private, which does not unsend a JPEG.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: She flipped the payment to private after the JPEG hit the family chat.

social.video_title: Rent help became a loan with interest in the chat — Part 1/2
social.description: March Venmo, pay when you can, a sudden APR. Linda hates screenshots. Would you have captioned it?

parts.text: I paid nothing extra. Amber deleted the interest speech. I paid the $400 when I could, in June, with a note that said not a loan, as discussed. The chat moved on to recipes. I archive money notes now. Private is not a time machine. Family can gift or they can underwrite. They should pick before March. I picked the JPEG.

social.video_title: June repayment used her original words — Part 2/2
social.description: No interest, not-a-loan note, recipes resume. Was thanks a contract?
